passage:
I'm Eshaan. Last year I got an offer for a design course in Pune. Papa had other plans: engineering, like him, like his father. He'd taken a loan for my coaching. When I told him about the design course, he didn't shout. He just said, "So all that was for nothing." Mummy said, "He means we gave up so much for our son, beta." My brother Mridul told me later that Papa sat on the terrace till midnight.
I understood it then. To them, my choice wasn't about a course. It felt like I was saying no to everything they had done for me, and to the family way. I wasn't. I just wanted to draw. But it took us months to hear each other.

qa.q: What course did Eshaan get an offer for?
qa.a: He got an offer for a design course in Pune.

qa.q: What was Papa feeling when he said, "So all that was for nothing"?
qa.a: He seemed hurt and let down, feeling that Eshaan's choice rejected the loan, the coaching and the family tradition.

qa.q: What could Eshaan have said to ease the clash?
qa.a: He could have told his parents clearly that he valued their sacrifice and wasn't rejecting them, and explained why design mattered to him.

qa.q: How did Mridul experience the conflict?
qa.a: He was a worried witness in between, noticing their father sitting on the terrace till midnight and later telling Eshaan.

grounding: It shows a young man's choice of course clashing with his father's plan, which carries sacrifice and expectation, so the choice feels like rejecting the family.

passage:
Supervisor's note, summer internship programme.
Aditi, one of our best interns, received a full-time offer from our Bengaluru office today. At lunch I saw her on the phone in the corridor. I could hear her mother's voice rising. Aditi kept saying, "Ma, it's just a job, it's not about leaving you." Her mother said something about the shop, and her father's health, and how they had planned for Aditi to join the family business in Nashik. Aditi came back with red eyes. She told me, "They think I'm choosing strangers over them."
I told her she didn't have to decide today. I gave her the HR contact to ask for more time, and suggested she talk with her parents face to face.
— Ishita, programme lead

qa.q: Which office did Aditi get an offer from?
qa.a: She got a full-time offer from the Bengaluru office.

qa.q: What does Aditi's line "They think I'm choosing strangers over them" show about her feelings?
qa.a: It shows she feels misunderstood and sad, since her parents take her job choice as rejecting the family and its plans.

qa.q: What support did Ishita offer at this stage?
qa.a: Ishita told Aditi there was no need to decide today, helped Aditi ask for more time and suggested a face-to-face talk, giving room for a calmer conversation.

qa.q: How might Aditi's mother see the Bengaluru offer?
qa.a: She may see it as a loss of the future they planned together, and worry about the shop and her husband's health without Aditi.

grounding: It illustrates a clash over a job in another city, where the family's plan and sacrifice make the young woman's choice feel like a rejection.
